subject: Short-window capacity ladder + blended overrun holdback request
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@brightapps.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Short-window capacity ladder request for upcoming launch

Hi Jonas / Ben,

Quick one — we have a paid customer launch scheduled for 2026-06-01 (internal feature flag goes live at 09:00 PT). The engineering team is projecting a 36–48 hour spike in QPS that will push our usual token rates ~3x for the first two days.

We want to avoid a hard throttle during the launch window and were hoping Redwood could provide: 
- temporary capacity ladder (short-window uplift) for 72 hours starting 2026-06-01 08:00 PT; target uplift = 2.5x baseline concurrent throughput
- a blended overrun holdback rate for any tokens beyond our committed slab so our teams don’t see a sudden 4–5x bill shock

Attached is a draft PO placeholder and a pre-launch usage snapshot (qps snapshot from May 22). Can you share whether Redwood can: (a) hold a blended overrun rate for a short window, and (b) give us an emergency escalation path if we exceed headroom?

We’re flexible on a small premium for the temporary uplift but would like to lock the overrun rate (even if limited to a token cap) to avoid surprises.

Thanks — Maya

--
Maya Singh
Head of Platform, BrightApps
maya@brightapps.com

Attachment(s): BrightApps_PO_20260523.pdf, qps_usage_snapshot_may22.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@brightapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-window capacity ladder request for upcoming launch

Maya — thanks for the heads-up and the snapshot. We can support short-window uplifts like this, and we have a couple of standard ways to avoid invoice shock while keeping capacity predictable. Proposed approach below (internal notes in parentheses):

1) Temporary headroom: reserve a provisional 2.5x uplift for a 72-hour window starting 2026-06-01 08:00 PT. If execution needs to start earlier we can shift the window by up to 12 hours with notice. (Ops: will gate on available dedicated pools)

2) Blended overrun rate: rather than pure PAYG, we can offer a blended overrun rate at 25% off PAYG for up to a 120M-token cap during that 72-hour window. Once the cap is hit, normal PAYG applies unless we trigger an emergency escalation. (Finance/legal: will need PO + amendment)

3) Escalation & throttles: if consumption threatens platform stability, Redwood may apply short, automated soft-throttles and simultaneously notify ops — we’ll provide a 10-minute heads-up where possible. For BrightApps, we can set a non-blocking mitigation policy for this window (i.e., progressive shedding rather than hard stop).

Next steps from our side: Ben will prep a short amendment (pricing + token cap + PO acceptance flow), Laura will confirm invoice timing and whether this can be billed as a one-off true-up on next month’s invoice. Markus — can you confirm capacity availability for the requested dates?

If this all sounds good Maya, send the signed PO and we’ll push an amendment through DocuSign. I attached a proposed amendment template (proposed_amendment_v1.docx) to speed things up.

Cheers,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment(s): proposed_amendment_v1.docx
From: Maya Singh <maya@brightapps.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-window capacity ladder request for upcoming launch

Thanks — that framework should work. A couple quick confirmations from our finance/ops side: 
- BrightApps can accept the 25% blended discount on PAYG up to a 120M-token cap for the 72-hour window.
- We can get a PO over to you today (attached placeholder). Please confirm the invoice date — we prefer a single true-up on the June invoice vs multiple line items.

One more ask: is there any possibility of a small, one-time commercial concession (10% credit on overage spend above the 120M cap) if we unexpectedly go materially over during launch? We’re committing to post-launch traffic smoothing and a follow-up review; that concession would be very helpful to get legal/finance to sign today.

Quoting your earlier message for context:
> Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-window capacity ladder request for upcoming launch — amendment & DocuSign

Maya — appreciate the quick turnaround. Final confirmation below and action items: 

- We will provision the 2.5x uplift for the 72-hour window starting 2026-06-01 08:00 PT.
- Blended overrun = PAYG less 25% up to 120M tokens.
- One-time goodwill credit: Redwood will provide a 10% credit on any overage spend above the 120M cap for amounts attributable to launch day spikes (we’ll reconcile against logs during post-launch review). Credit will be applied as a contra-line on the July invoice.

I’ve created the amendment and sent it via DocuSign: https://docusign.net/BRI/amendment/00234 — please route to your legal and sign before 2026-05-31 to guarantee capacity hold. Once signed, Laura will convert the PO and the uplift will be scheduled in our provisioning system.

Ben/Laura/Markus: please confirm you’ve queued the amendment and have capacity reserved. I’ll follow up with ops runbook (short checklist for the BrightApps SREs) and a post-launch review slot for the week of 2026-06-07.

Thanks — looking forward to helping BrightApps have a clean launch.

Best,
Jonas
